title: Align Skill tool with the TS baseline
objective: Implement all Skill improvements identified by the per-tool subagent report so the Go clone matches the original TypeScript tool in public contract, runtime logic, robustness, state lifecycle, and tests.

context.problem: Go Skill covers the smallest happy path of looking up an installed SKILL.md, substituting arguments, and returning prompt text, but it is not yet TS-equivalent as a runtime tool. The largest parity gaps are around model-visible output shape, new-message/context injection, permission ask/allow/deny lifecycle, forked execution, allowed-tools/model/effort propagation, source discovery, MCP skill wiring, shell/hook support, invoked-skill compaction state, and exact skill-name resolution. Existing Go tests cover local helpers and basic manager behavior, but they do not yet protect the end-to-end query-loop, post-compact, forked-agent, MCP, hook, or conditional-discovery contracts that make TS Skill behave like a lifecycle tool rather than a plain text expander.

parallelization_notes: Can be assigned to an implementation subagent after listed dependencies are available. Avoid running concurrently with another task that owns the same files.

improvement_points.title: Skill output is returned as tool_result text instead of TS data plus injected messages
improvement_points.description: TS Skill returns structured data and injects the rendered skill prompt as new assistant/user messages while the model-facing tool_result text remains a short launcher/completion message. Go returns the rendered skill body directly in ToolResult.Content and puts status fields into metadata. Because Go metadata is not serialized into provider tool_result blocks, downstream runtime state and model-visible output differ materially from TS.

improvement_points.title: Skill-specific permission ask/allow/deny lifecycle is not enforced before content exposure
improvement_points.description: TS checks Skill permissions against deny rules, allow rules, safe frontmatter properties, remote-skill exceptions, and interactive ask suggestions before loading unsafe skill content into the conversation. Go computes an internal permissionDecision metadata value, but for the `ask` path it still prepares and returns the skill content. The normal outer permission handler sees only the generic Skill tool call and is not wired into Skill frontmatter semantics.

improvement_points.title: allowed-tools, model, and reasoning effort modifiers are not applied to the next loop like TS
improvement_points.description: TS Skill returns a contextModifier that mutates the next execution context: allowedTools are injected into toolPermissionContext, model is switched with the 1m suffix logic, and reasoning effort is propagated. Go records allowed tools/model/effort in metadata and optionally calls an AllowedToolsApplier, but the applier is not wired in SetupRegistry and its cleanup is deferred until Execute returns, before the next model turn can use it.

improvement_points.title: Fork-context skills are marked as forked but no sub-agent is run
improvement_points.description: TS treats `context: fork` as a distinct execution mode: it prepares a forked command context, starts a sub-agent with progress reporting, waits for the result, returns the agent id and result text, and clears invoked skills for the child agent. Go only changes status metadata to `forked` and appends a textual note, but still returns the local prepared content directly.

improvement_points.title: Skill source loading and conditional activation do not match TS
improvement_points.description: TS loads managed, user, project, additional, plugin, bundled, built-in-plugin, legacy command, dynamic, and conditional path-based skills with explicit ordering, realpath deduplication, policy gates, and deepest-path precedence. Go loads direct child SKILL.md directories from a narrower default dir set, merges MCP prompts after on-disk skills, exposes path-conditional skills immediately, and leaves ActivateConditionalForPath as a no-op. Go file-read dynamic discovery also searches a different set of directories and does not mirror TS cwd-bound/gitignore behavior.

improvement_points.title: MCP skills support exists locally but is not wired to runtime MCP skill discovery
improvement_points.description: TS Skill merges MCP prompt commands from AppState and the command loader uses MCP skill fetch/list plumbing. TS also marks MCP-created commands so they do not run local shell command injections. Go has an MCP prompt registration helper, but repository search evidence shows no production call into it, so runtime MCP prompts are not guaranteed to appear as Skill choices.

improvement_points.title: Inline shell command expansion inside SKILL.md is not implemented
improvement_points.description: TS executes `!` shell command injections in skill prompts for non-MCP skills, using the skill's base directory, shell frontmatter, and allowed-tools permission context. Go stores shell metadata and performs argument/path substitutions, but PrepareSkillContent explicitly does not execute shell command substitutions.

improvement_points.title: Skill hooks are not parsed into runtime skill state or registered one-shot like TS
improvement_points.description: TS parses hooks from skill frontmatter and registers session-scoped hooks when a prompt slash command/skill is invoked, subject to hook permission policy, with one-shot cleanup. Go frontmatter parsing keeps hooks only in raw metadata and the Skill struct does not expose or register them during SkillTool execution.

improvement_points.title: Invoked-skill session, toolUseID, content/path, and compaction state are incomplete
improvement_points.description: TS records invoked skills with name, path, full content, invokedAt, and agentId; compaction reinjects recent invoked skill content and forked execution clears child-agent entries. Go snapshots only name/toolUseID/source, and normal loop context values are not read by SkillTool because it uses private context keys rather than the loop ToolExecutionContext. Post-compact attachments therefore list skill names instead of carrying the TS skill content/path context.

improvement_points.title: Skill name validation and lookup are stricter than TS and do not cover aliases/display names
improvement_points.description: TS trims names, strips a leading slash, validates remote canonical names when relevant, and then uses command lookup that can match the command name, displayed/user-facing names, and aliases. Legacy command loading can produce nested namespace names. Go rejects path separators, path traversal, and any colon form except exactly `plugin:skill` before lookup, and the manager cache is keyed by the canonical skill name only.

improvement_points.title: Usage ranking and prompt budget controls are only partially aligned
improvement_points.description: TS records skill usage on invocation and prompt slash command processing, and the skill listing prompt honors SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET. Go has a usage store and prompt budget helper, but SetupRegistry does not wire the usage store into SkillTool, query-loop listing does not use the ranking store, and the Go char budget helper uses static defaults rather than the TS environment override.

improvement_points.title: Remote canonical skills are not implemented despite matching error code surface
improvement_points.description: TS has an experimental remote canonical skill path that validates canonical names, discovers remote skills, fetches SKILL.md, strips frontmatter, substitutes session/base-dir variables, records invoked skill content, and emits telemetry. Go defines a remote-not-discovered error code, but the normal SkillTool path has no remote canonical discovery/load branch.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align Skill tool output contract and injected message flow
acceptance_criteria: Inline Skill result exposes success, commandName, status, and optional allowedTools/model fields in a structured Go contract or equivalent provider-visible data path.
Rendered skill prompt is delivered through ToolResult.NewMessages or the query-loop equivalent, not as the primary tool_result text.
Tool result text for inline skills matches the TS launcher shape.
Existing content-block serialization does not drop the injected skill content.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Change Skill execution so inline skills return TS-like structured data/status and inject rendered skill prompt content through NewMessages instead of raw ToolResult.Content. Preserve a short model-facing tool result such as `Launching skill: <name>` and add tests that assert the serialized transcript shape.

implementation_subtasks.title: Implement Skill-specific permission ask/allow/deny lifecycle
acceptance_criteria: Skills with deny-matched unsafe properties are blocked before PrepareSkillContent.
Skills requiring ask do not expose rendered content until permission is granted.
Allow rules and safe-property-only skills bypass ask consistently with TS.
SetupRegistry wires the Skill permission context from the active runtime instead of leaving AllowRules/DenyRules empty.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Bridge Skill frontmatter-aware permission checks into the normal permission runtime. Deny must stop before prompt content is prepared; ask must surface a permission request with TS-like rule suggestions; safe-property skills can auto-allow.

implementation_subtasks.title: Apply skill allowed-tools, model, and effort to runtime context
acceptance_criteria: Skill allowed-tools apply to subsequent tool permission checks for the right session/toolUseID and are cleaned up after their intended lifecycle.
Skill model selection affects the next model turn and uses existing parent-model suffix logic.
Skill effort affects the next model turn where Go supports reasoning effort.
No context leak occurs across unrelated sessions or concurrent tool invocations.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Implement the TS contextModifier equivalent for Go Skill. Skill allowedTools should become active for the relevant tool_use_id/turn, model metadata should switch the next main-loop model with the existing 1m suffix behavior, and effort should propagate to the next model invocation.

implementation_subtasks.title: Implement forked skill execution
acceptance_criteria: A fork-context skill runs through the Go agent/sub-agent path rather than returning local prompt content.
Forked Skill result contains status=forked, agentId, and result text comparable to TS.
Progress/result failures are reported with forked-skill error metadata.
Invoked-skill state associated with the child agent is cleared or scoped after completion.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Replace the current `status=forked` placeholder with real sub-agent execution for skills whose context is `fork`, including prompt preparation, allowed-tools/model context, progress/result handling, agent id metadata, and cleanup of child invoked-skill state.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align skill loading, ordering, dynamic discovery, and conditional paths
acceptance_criteria: Default skill dirs include the TS-equivalent managed/user/project/additional sources supported by the Go app.
Path-conditional skills are hidden until ActivateConditionalForPath matches a path.
Dynamic file-read discovery is cwd-bounded and gitignore-aware like TS.
Ordering and duplicate/shadow handling are covered with fixture tests.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Bring Go SkillManager discovery and listing behavior in line with TS: source directories, ordering/shadowing, managed/additional/plugin/bundled/legacy support where applicable, dynamic discovery boundaries, gitignore skipping, and path-conditional activation rather than unconditional listing.

implementation_subtasks.title: Wire MCP skills into SkillManager runtime
acceptance_criteria: Runtime MCP prompt skills appear in SkillManager.All/Get with source metadata equivalent to TS loadedFrom=mcp.
MCP skills can be invoked through SkillTool and produce TS-like output/newMessages.
MCP skills never execute local shell prompt injections.
MCP refresh/removal updates the manager without stale entries.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Connect the runtime MCP client prompt/skill discovery path to skills.RegisterMCPPrompts or a manager-owned equivalent, preserve MCP source metadata, and ensure MCP skills are included in Skill lookup/listing while local shell expansion stays disabled for MCP sources.

implementation_subtasks.title: Implement TS-compatible shell command expansion for skill prompts
acceptance_criteria: Non-MCP skill content with shell injections expands to command output like TS.
Shell expansion honors the skill Shell frontmatter and base directory.
Shell expansion is blocked or asks according to Skill permission lifecycle.
MCP-sourced skills skip local shell execution.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Execute inline `!` shell command substitutions in non-MCP skill content with the skill base directory, shell configuration, and allowed-tools/permission context matching TS. Preserve current argument and session substitutions.

implementation_subtasks.title: Parse and register skill hooks with one-shot lifecycle
acceptance_criteria: Skill frontmatter hooks parse into typed Skill fields.
Invoking a skill registers hooks for the current session only when policy permits.
Registered hooks are removed after their intended one-shot lifecycle.
Unsafe hook frontmatter participates in Skill permission checks.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Promote hooks from raw frontmatter into the Skill model and register them when the skill is invoked, subject to the Go hook permission/trust model, with one-shot cleanup equivalent to TS registerSkillHooks.

implementation_subtasks.title: Preserve invoked skill content/path and loop context through compaction
acceptance_criteria: Normal Skill invocations use loop session id and tool_use_id instead of fallback UUID/private-only context keys.
Invocation snapshots include rendered content, skill path, invokedAt, source, and agent id where applicable.
Post-compact attachments include recent invoked skill content/path sorted most-recent-first with truncation behavior.
Forked child-agent invoked skill entries are scoped and cleared according to the fork lifecycle.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Consume the normal loop ToolExecutionContext in SkillTool, record real session/toolUseID plus rendered skill content/path/invokedAt/agentId, and update post-compact attachments to reinject recent invoked skill content like TS.

implementation_subtasks.title: Align skill name validation, aliases, display names, and legacy namespaces
acceptance_criteria: Leading slash handling matches TS Execute behavior.
Aliases and display/user-facing names resolve to the same skill as canonical name.
Supported legacy namespaced commands with multiple colons can resolve where TS would load them.
Invalid path-like names still fail with Skill validation errors.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Relax Go pre-lookup validation to match TS, then implement lookup indexes for aliases/display names and supported legacy nested namespace names. Keep path traversal/path separator rejection where TS-equivalent safety requires it, but do not reject TS-valid names before lookup.

implementation_subtasks.title: Wire skill usage ranking and prompt budget environment override
acceptance_criteria: SetupRegistry wires a shared SkillUsageStore into SkillTool.
Skill invocations update usage state in production runtime.
Skill listing order/truncation uses usage ranking where TS does.
SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET overrides Go skill listing char budget.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Assign a production UsageStore to SkillTool, apply usage ranking to skill listings where TS does, and make Go skill listing budget respect SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET.

implementation_subtasks.title: Add remote canonical skill discovery and execution path
acceptance_criteria: Canonical remote names are detected and validated before local manager lookup.
Discovered remote SKILL.md content is fetched, normalized, and injected through the same output/newMessages path as inline skills.
Remote invocation records invoked-skill content/path/source for compaction.
Remote-not-discovered and invalid-remote-name errors match the Go/TS error-code contract.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Implement the TS experimental remote canonical branch for Go if the Go product intends to support canonical remote skills: validation, discovery, SKILL.md fetch/cache, frontmatter stripping, base-dir/session substitution, telemetry/state recording, and TS-like not-discovered errors.

risks: Some subtasks touch shared runtime surfaces; coordinate with foundation tasks to avoid incompatible local adapters.
non_goals: Do not make unrelated behavior changes outside this tool unless required by a listed dependency.
notes_for_assignee: Start by adding or updating parity fixtures, then implement the smallest vertical slice that makes a failing fixture pass. Keep TS evidence lines in comments or test names where useful.
